exposure: Planned mode of delivery (vaginal vs cesarean)
outcome: Major adverse outcomes (death, cerebral palsy, necrotizing enterocolitis, chronic renal, heart, or lung disease)
Minor adverse outcomes (learning disability, speech therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy)
cohort: Twin pregnancies delivered at or after 34 weeks
finding: Planned vaginal delivery with active management of the second stage of labor in twin pregnancies >34 weeks was not associated with adverse childhood outcomes compared to planned cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal delivery with active management of the second stage of labor in twin pregnancies >34 weeks was not associated with adverse childhood outcomes compared to planned cesarean delivery.
